title: tier record
description: What one inference tier was measured to do. Contains no model name in any field the router reads: `serves` is provenance for a human, and every routing decision is taken from the measured fields. A field whose value was not measured is null, never zero and never a published figure -- this deployment has seen an engine advertise 7-14x more reusable cache than it had and a rate card price a model 17x wrong.

schema_version.description: The record format. Present so a future reader can tell what it is looking at rather than guessing from which fields exist.

id.description: Stable key the router uses. Opaque; not parsed.

serves.description: Human-readable provenance only. The router must not branch on anything in here.

provenance.description: Where the numbers came from, so a decision is reproducible from versioned inputs.

adapter.description: Protocol facts, measured separately from task ability. Conflating the two cost one tier 42% of its actions once.

compliance.description: Fractions of parsed steps, from a measured run.

restrictions.description: Combinations the endpoint refuses, as capability facts rather than as 400s discovered at runtime.

price_card.description: Per request shape, because the cache discount attaches to the shape and not to the text: identical content sent as one long message hit 0% where a growing conversation hit 99.9%.

source.description: Catalog and retrieval, or the measurement that produced it. Published figures are inadmissible where a measured one exists.

cached_in.description: null when the tier does not report cached tokens. Never coerced to zero: unmeasured is not free.

hourly_fixed_usd.description: Non-null makes this tier's effective rate max(token rates, hourly / realised tasks per hour), recomputed hourly.

reusable_cache_tokens.description: Measured by interposing traffic between populate and reuse, not read from the engine's advertised capacity.

latency.description: A distribution, because chains stack tails and a mean hides the arrangement that misses its SLO. Superseded per family by `families[<family>].latency` where that exists, because latency turned out to be a property of the tier-and-family pair rather than of the tier.

concurrency_when_measured.description: A latency figure taken at low concurrency is optimistic in exactly the regime where the cost figure is realistic.

reliability.description: The term that reordered the arrangements. Cost of a call is bill + p/(1-p) * mean spend sunk before death, so an unreliable tier that dies late is dearer than its bill.

families.description: Per traffic family, the measured outcome and whether this tier is nested under the family's reference tier. Nesting is a per-family, per-pair property re-certified at admission, never a global assumption.

suite.description: The frozen benchmark set and its selection rule.

runs_per_item.description: One run measures an episode, not a capability.

counterexamples.description: Items this tier solved and the reference did not, i.e. `paired_vs_reference.candidate_only`. Kept for readability. It is NOT a disqualification: a crossover is evidence that the reference is not sufficient for the family, not that the candidate is unsafe, and one crossover in twenty items is a coin flip. Nesting is used only to decide whether a chain may be constructed at all.

cohort.description: Hash of the exact item set this outcome was measured on. Two records can only be compared as a pair if these match: without it there is no way to know the same items were given to both tiers, and a paired bound computed across different item sets is not a bound. When `evidence` is present, the cohort is derived from it (see `evidence`) and this field is redundant; a hand-written value here is never trusted over the derived one.

evidence.description: Where the per-item observations live, in place of a hand-computed `paired_vs_reference` summary. Mutually exclusive with `paired_vs_reference` -- exactly one of the two is required -- because a family whose outcome can be recomputed from underlying observations must not also carry a second, independently hand-written number that the recomputation could silently disagree with. `digest` is checked against the artifact's own content on every read, not only at write time, so a file that changed after this record was written is caught rather than trusted.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the JSONL artifact. Its filename carries the first 16 hex characters of its own content digest, so the name is fixed once the bytes are and a merged or edited file cannot keep it.

digest.description: Full content digest of the artifact, `sha256:<64 hex>`. Independent of the 16-character prefix in the filename: this is the record's own claim about which bytes it is evidence for, checked against the artifact on every load rather than assumed from a name that merely looks right.

paired_vs_reference.description: The 2x2 against the family's reference tier on the same cohort, hand-computed from a comparison that was run once and never stored per item. A paired experiment reported as two marginal rates throws away exactly the information that decides the comparison: 14 of 20 against 20 of 20 has a point difference of -0.30, but all six discordant pairs favour the reference and the lower bound is far below that. Mutually exclusive with `evidence`: a family carrying per-item observations derives this shape rather than storing a second, independently hand-written copy of it. Records dated on or after the evidence cutover (see `tierbook.policy.EVIDENCE_CUTOVER_DATE`) may not use this field at all.

accounting_boundary.description: What `bill_usd` covers, so it is never added to a modelled surcharge for the same spend. Default meaning: the items that produced a usable episode, with attempts that died on transport excluded -- those are priced by `reliability.mean_sunk_usd` instead. One boundary, not both.

latency.description: Latency for this tier ON THIS FAMILY. The second family measured here made it clear that latency is a property of the pair and not of the tier: the same tier took 94 seconds a task on one family and 13 on another. A per-family figure supersedes the top-level one.

eligibility.description: Hard constraints, checked before any cost arithmetic.

max_requests_per_second.description: The cheapest tier can simply be unable to take the load. Null means unmeasured, which eligibility treats as unconstrained -- so measure it before assigning a family to a tier at volume.

measurement_target.description: Exactly what was measured, pinned. The rule stays model-agnostic; the record must not: a tier record that does not say what it measured silently describes a different system after the provider's next quiet upgrade.

claim.description: What this record's outcomes are a claim ABOUT. Structural rather than a note, because the difference between 'this tier solved the task' and 'this tier agreed with a strong model' is the difference between a routable measurement and a diagnostic.

kind.description: correctness: an independent mechanism decided. reference_agreement: another model's output was the standard, which does not estimate correctness and can never assign.

oracle.description: What decided each outcome. `independent_of_candidate` is the field the compiler gates on: a standard produced by a model that is also a candidate scores that candidate perfectly by construction.

checker_id.description: Version of the mechanism, so a record says which checker judged it.

existed_before_candidate_output.description: A check written after seeing the output is not a check. On one corpus here the judging tests were absent from the checkout by construction, which is what made the in-tree tests anti-correlated with solving.

generator.description: For a model-generated standard: which model, which revision, which prompt digest, when. Recorded so the same checkpoint cannot appear as both standard and candidate under two names.

coverage.description: For a benchmark extracted from logs: how much of the log population had an admissible check. A measurement over the checkable subset says nothing about the rest, and the compiler must not extrapolate.
